cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend, because we're hitting the road with Jesus and His disciples. The day of His ascension is getting close. And Jesus sets out for Jerusalem.

cards.question: As the day of His ascension gets close, Jesus ___ sets out for Jerusalem.

cards.text: Jesus sends messengers on ahead into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him. It's calling ahead so the room's ready when you pull in. Smart.

cards.question: Jesus' messengers reach the Samaritan village. How do the people there respond to Him?
Why does the Samaritan village refuse to welcome Jesus?

answers.text: They had never heard of Him

cards.text: James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, see all this. And they come to Jesus with an offer that is, uh… a LOT.

cards.question: James and John ask, “Lord, do You want us to call down ___ from heaven to consume them?”
True or false: Jesus tells James and John to go ahead and call it down on the Samaritan village.

cards.text: Then Jesus and His disciples just go on to another village. Friend, if somebody doesn't hold the elevator for me, I'm still practicing my speech about it in the shower that NIGHT.
As they're walking along the road, someone says to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.” WHEREVER. That is a big word, friend.

cards.question: Jesus answers the man who says he'll follow Him wherever: “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” What is Jesus warning him about?

answers.text: Following Him means no settled home
The road ahead has wild animals
The man needs a house first

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to another man and says, “Follow Me.” The man says, “Lord, first…” and oh, I KNOW that word, friend, every snooze button on earth has heard it a thousand times.

cards.question: Jesus tells a man, “Follow Me.” The man replies, “Lord, first let me go and ___ my father.”

cards.text: But Jesus tells him, “Let the dead bury their own dead.” And then Jesus hands this man a job.

cards.question: Instead of burying his father first, what does Jesus tell this man to go do?

cards.text: Then still another man speaks up: “I will follow You, Lord; but first…” There's that word AGAIN.

cards.question: True or false: This third man asks Jesus to let him first say farewell to his family.

cards.text: Jesus answers him with a picture from the field: a man who puts his hand to the plow.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, what does the man at the plow do that makes him not fit for the kingdom of God?

cards.text: Then Jesus declares, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” Friend, I tried driving forward while staring in the rearview mirror once, and I met a hedge. Up close.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 7 quotes "Lord, do You want us to call down ___ from heaven to consume them?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the BSB word "resolutely" against "reluctantly" and "secretly." Card 1 gives nothing about how Jesus sets out, so this tests wording the baker hasn't seen and comes down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke ("It's calling ahead so the room's ready when you pull in. Smart.") reads as a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says "call it down," and "it" points back to the fire answer on card 7, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: No card ever says that Jesus turned and rebuked James and John (Luke 9:55). The true/false answer only shows that He didn't tell them to go ahead, so the baker misses an important detail. Card 9 then jumps straight to the next village.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke has Papa Dorin holding a grudge: he rehearses a speech in the shower all night because someone didn't hold the elevator. This goes against his godly character, which never holds a grudge.

rule.text: Godly character. He never holds a grudge, and his humor reflects kindness and forgiveness.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin tells a personal story about riding an elevator and showering. Both add new experiences to his life, outside the Millers' kitchen, the drawer and his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The snooze-button joke treats the man's request to bury his father as stalling. The text gives no reason for his request, and the joke laughs at a grieving son instead of looking at his situation with respect. The comparison also doesn't click: people don't say "first" to a snooze button.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the man's line ("bury" against "visit" and "help"). Nothing told so far points to burial, so this is a wording guess, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he once drove a car and hit a hedge. That adds a new experience to his backstory, outside his bakery and his established world.
